name: Aetius of Antioch
otherNames: Aetius the Godless ("Atheus"), the nickname given him by the Arians
knownFor: A sharp-tongued Arian logician who taught that the Son is unlike the Father, founding the Anomoean party; even the Arians cast him out.
dates: Active from about 350; died at Constantinople, about 367
place: From Coele-Syria; taught at Antioch and Alexandria

keyWorks.title: The Syntagmation
keyWorks.about: a short book of logical propositions arguing the Son is unlike the Father, kept inside Epiphanius's Panarion 76, which copies it out to refute it

traces: The Anomoeans, later called Eunomians after his pupil Eunomius of Cyzicus, who carried his teaching on.
remembered: Socrates of Constantinople records the nickname his own side gave him, Atheus, the godless one.
At the Council of Constantinople in 360 his own party deposed him from the diaconate to satisfy the emperor.

uncertain: His life is told mostly through partisans. Philostorgius, who praised him, gives the story of the poor goldsmith who rose by logic; his history survives only in a hostile summary by Photius. Socrates, Sozomen and Epiphanius, who opposed him, tell the rest.

He leaned on Aristotle's Categories, Socrates says, and framed arguments that even fellow Arians could not follow, so they called him a heretic. Whether this was depth or vain subtlety, his friends and his foes disagreed.
The years of his birth and death are not given in a held source. Philostorgius places his death at Constantinople, after Julian had given him land on Lesbos.
